//: Composite indexes required by Dhakker.
The assistant proxy (assistant-proxy/worker.js, queryFirestoreSupplications)
issues an ARRAY_CONTAINS_ANY query on the language-appropriate tag field
together with equality filters on isActive and verificationStatus.
Firestore requires a composite index for that combination, and the query
FAILS without it. Retrieval failure degrades safely (the assistant returns
its deterministic 'no approved source' response rather than erroring), so a
missing index looks like 'the assistant never finds anything' rather than a
crash — deploy these before expecting grounded answers.
Field order matters: equality filters first, array-contains last.
Deploy with:  firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes

//: The three pilgrim-facing retrieval paths, all carrying the same
read gate: isActive == true, verificationStatus == 'verified',
revokedAt == null.
Those three filters are NOT optional. firestore.rules evaluates the
read condition against every document a query matches, and rejects
the whole query if any matched document fails. A query missing one
of them matches an unverified record and dies with
permission-denied — it does not quietly return less.
revokedAt is queried with an equality filter on null, which does
NOT match documents where the field is absent. Every writer must
therefore write it explicitly: the importer forces revokedAt: null,
and the admin console writes it too. A record created without it is
invisible to the app while looking correct in the console.
Which of these are strictly REQUIRED, stated honestly: Firestore
serves multiple equality filters by merging single-field indexes, so
the zoneKey and zoneId variants would work without a composite index
and are declared for predictable performance. The appliesToZoneKeys
variant is genuinely required — array-contains combined with
equality filters cannot be served without one.
A missing or still-building index fails the query with
failed-precondition. getSupplicationsByZone no longer swallows that:
it records a SupplicationQueryFailure and logs a diagnostic, because
an empty list is indistinguishable from "no duas in this zone".
Deployment order matters — see docs/DEPLOYMENT_ORDER.md.
